clue.text: Turn on illuminations in seaside resort, say

indicators.note: say tells us the resort's name is to be taken as spoken, giving a word sounding the same

parts.note: Brighton is a seaside resort on England's south coast

explanation.surface: A town on the coast switches on its famous seafront lights.
explanation.walkthrough: BRIGHTON, a resort on the English south coast, sounds like the answer. The illuminations suggest Blackpool, but they are the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Switching on lights makes a place lighter, which is to brighten it.

clue.text: It's taking less time to put monarch in the picture

parts.note: with put, to put someone in the picture is to brief them
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the reigning queen

explanation.surface: An aide must give the queen a quick update on the situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put ... in the picture' means BRIEF, and ER (the Queen) is the one briefed. Read whole, 'to put monarch in the picture' is 'brief ER'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something shorter in duration than another lasts less time, a comparative adjective.

clue.text: Involve whip in story one parliamentarian covers

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
MP is a Member of Parliament; covers just says this sits on top in the down entry

indicators.note: in places the whip word within the story word

parts.note: a lie is a story, a falsehood
a cat is a whip, as in cat-o'-nine-tails

explanation.surface: A party whip is dragged into a scandal hushed up by one member of parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' sets the whip inside the story, giving LICATE. The surface's party whip, who keeps MPs in line, is a cat-o'-nine-tails here.
explanation.definitionFit: To implicate someone is to show them to be involved, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Rush hour — nonetheless, runs? Yes

indicators.note: nonetheless read as none-the-less says nought, a zero or O, is removed from the word before it

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for runs in cricket scoring
yup is an informal yes

explanation.surface: At rush hour do people still run? Yes, they do.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'nonetheless' as 'none the less': nought, the letter O, is dropped. R is runs on a cricket scorecard.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurry up is a phrasal verb meaning to go faster, the same as rush.

clue.text: Needed when firm's in money trouble?

definitions.text: Needed when firm's in money trouble?

indicators.note: in places the firm abbreviation within the rearranged letters
trouble suggests the letters of money are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: Co, for company, is a firm

explanation.surface: Belt-tightening is called for when a company is short of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' makes ENOMY, and 'in' sets the firm after its first letter. As a whole, the clue describes what a struggling business needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting spending is thrift, the remedy for a business in financial difficulty.

clue.text: Remarkable archbishop is back

indicators.note: back tells us the archbishop's name and the word is together are read from right to left

parts.note: Cosmo Lang was Archbishop of Canterbury in the 1930s

explanation.surface: An outstanding churchman has returned to his post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns LANG + IS, giving SIGNAL. Lang was Archbishop of Canterbury when Edward VIII abdicated in 1936.
explanation.definitionFit: A signal achievement is a notable, striking one, so the adjective is a synonym.

clue.text: Mary's upset about soldiers arguing on premises

indicators.note: about places the reversed name around the soldiers
in a down clue, upset says the name is turned upside down, reading backwards

parts.note: Molly is a pet form of Mary, and the 's gives the S
GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: Mary gets upset with some soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses the name to SYLLOM, and 'about' wraps that round the soldiers. Molly is a familiar form of Mary.
explanation.definitionFit: A deductive argument draws a conclusion from two premises, a classic form of logic.

clue.text: American investigating on foot? So it might appear.

definitions.text: on foot? So it might appear.

explanation.surface: A US private eye goes about his inquiries on foot.
explanation.walkthrough: The second part reads the word literally: a gumshoe is a rubber-soled shoe, so it is worn on the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A gumshoe is US slang for a detective, named for quiet rubber soles; literally the word is footwear made of gum.

clue.text: Old kingdom found as republic today

parts.note: Syria is a present-day republic in the Middle East

explanation.surface: An ancient kingdom is identified as a modern nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The ancient kingdom lay in Mesopotamia, near modern Syria, so the surface is nearly true.
explanation.definitionFit: Assyria was an ancient Mesopotamian empire, a kingdom of antiquity.

clue.text: Male prison's terribly inhuman

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters of the two words are badly jumbled into a new order

parts.note: the possessive ending adds no letter; it stands for 'is' in the surface

explanation.surface: A men's jail is a cruel and soulless place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges MALE + PRISON; the 's of prison's reads as 'is' and supplies nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impersonal lacks human warmth, which is a sense of inhuman.

clue.text: Screen dramatic entertainment for audience

indicators.note: for audience asks for the word as listeners would hear it, a sound-alike

parts.note: a masque is a courtly dramatic entertainment with music and dance

explanation.surface: A screen shows a play put on for the spectators.
explanation.walkthrough: MASQUE, the Renaissance court entertainment, is pronounced like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To mask something is to hide it from view, a synonym of screen as a verb.

clue.text: Just why, it's said, sponsor is unexpected source of help

parts.note: just means fair, as in a just decision

indicators.note: it's said marks that the word why is to be heard, giving a letter with the same sound

parts.note: the word why is spoken like the letter Y
a godmother sponsors a child at baptism

explanation.surface: Someone asks why a backer turns out to be an unlooked-for helper.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter Y is pronounced like 'why'. A godparent is said to sponsor the child at its christening.
explanation.definitionFit: In pantomime and fairy tale the magical helper appears from nowhere, so the phrase names any surprise benefactor.

clue.text: Cut, fold, and put on again

parts.note: to reap is to cut a crop
a ply is a fold or layer, as in two-ply

explanation.surface: Instructions for paper or fabric: cut it, fold it, and apply once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' and 'fold' look like craft instructions but each is a synonym piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To apply something a second time, such as paint or cream, is to lay it on once more.

clue.text: A thousand calories could make one very unhappy

indicators.note: could make suggests the letters can be formed into a new word

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Counting a thousand calories could make a dieter miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could make' rearranges M + CALORIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacrimose means tearful or weepy, a state of deep sadness.

clue.text: Fighting about one bill in drinking-place

indicators.note: about places the fighting word around the other pieces

parts.note: fighting is war
one is the Roman numeral I
neb is an old word for a bird's beak or bill

explanation.surface: A brawl breaks out over a tab in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the fighting round the rest. Bill here is a beak, not an invoice.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine bar is an establishment serving drinks, chiefly wine, so a place for drinking.

clue.text: Article on batting — West Indian without inspiration

indicators.note: without is used in its old sense of outside, so the Indian surrounds the rest

parts.note: a brave is a Native American warrior

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the article above what follows

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
in cricket, a side that is batting is in

explanation.surface: A cricket report says a West Indian batsman has no ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside, and 'on' sets the article above the batting word. 'West Indian' looks like a cricketer but splits into a compass point and a warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: A brainwave is a sudden clever idea, a flash of inspiration.

clue.text: Pupil given responsibility for head of department

explanation.surface: A senior pupil is put in charge of running a school department.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is French: a département of France is administered by an official with this title.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior schoolchild with duties is a monitor of this kind; in France the same title belongs to the government's chief administrator of a département.

clue.text: Disturbance, we hear, that one has to control in court

definitions.text: that one has to control in court

indicators.note: we hear says the word for disturbance is taken by sound alone

parts.note: a racket is a din or disturbance

explanation.surface: A noisy scene erupts that must be brought under control in a courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: The court is a tennis or squash court, not a law court.
explanation.definitionFit: A player in tennis or squash handles the bat with strings on a court.

clue.text: Something that can be got from conifer

definitions.text: Something that can be got from conifer

indicators.note: can be got from says the letters of the next word are taken and rearranged

explanation.surface: A product that comes from an evergreen tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be got from' rearranges the letters of CONIFER, and the cone does indeed come from the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Fir trees bear woody seed-cases, which come from a cone-bearing tree.

clue.text: Accept expression of affection

explanation.surface: Someone welcomes another with a warm hug.
explanation.definitionFit: To accept an idea is to take it to heart, and a hug is a gesture of love: both senses of the word.

clue.text: Blow up opponents at bridge? Great!

parts.note: East and North are opposing players in bridge
great means large

explanation.surface: A bridge player relishes blowing up the opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North-South partner against East-West, so E and N are opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow up a photograph is to make it bigger, a synonym.

clue.text: Some taboo steroids in extra dose

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An athlete takes banned drugs in an extra dose.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'in extra dose' as the definition; 'in' is a link word, and the definition is 'extra dose' alone, a noun like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A booster is a supplementary shot, such as a vaccine top-up.

clue.text: Sect members in German city starting to be repetitive

parts.note: Essen is a city in the Ruhr
the start of the city name is repeated, adding its first two letters again

explanation.surface: A religious group in a German city begins to sound repetitive.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening ES of ESSEN is repeated at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The Essenes were an ancient Jewish ascetic sect, so each was a member of that group.

clue.text: For example, 20'redheads

parts.note: a cardinal wears red robes, and cardinal is also a shade of red
heads are points, as with headlands jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: The clue reads as a puzzle about twenty people with red hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 refers to the answer at 20 down, ESSENES, whose letters are all E, S or N: compass directions. The clue was printed with an apostrophe-like mark after 20.
explanation.definitionFit: North, south, east and west are the compass bearings, and the letters at 20 down are made only of their initials.

clue.text: Whole ring is used in this sport

parts.note: a sum is a whole or total
the letter O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: The whole of the ring is used by competitors in this sport.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface fits the wrestling itself, fought within a circular ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Japanese wrestling between very heavy men is the sport meant.

clue.text: Excessively tax, so err in VAT, oddly

indicators.note: oddly says the following letters are set out in a strange new order

explanation.surface: Someone over-charges by making mistakes with value added tax.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT is the British value added tax, a sales tax.
explanation.definitionFit: To overstrain something is to push it beyond its limits, which is to tax it too heavily.

clue.text: Writer, English, contributed to long-standing column

indicators.note: contributed to says the letter goes into the column word, adding to it

parts.note: a stele is an ancient upright stone slab or pillar

explanation.surface: An English author wrote for a newspaper column that has run for years.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Steele co-founded The Tatler and The Spectator in the 18th century. The 'column' looks like journalism but is a standing stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Steele was an Irish-born essayist and playwright, an author.

clue.text: Still, we hear, without a successor

indicators.note: we hear tells us the synonym of still should be taken by its sound

parts.note: airless means still, with no breeze

explanation.surface: The heir is still not born, so the line has no successor.
explanation.walkthrough: AIRLESS (windless) is pronounced the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no heir means no one in line to inherit.
